assumptions: A GitHub repository is connected and holds the site's content as Markdown, MDX or static HTML. Other templating languages are reported as unsupported, never guessed at.
target_url is a published HTTPS page on the same site; link_budget is 1..5 and caps files touched, not links proposed.
Anchor phrases must already exist in a candidate page's prose. Frontmatter, headings, code, existing links, HTML attributes, MDX/JSX syntax and bare URLs are not prose.
Run success establishes that a pull request or an explicit no-change result was delivered. It does not establish that a link is worth making; that needs the rubric below.
Fixtures are synthetic. A live run needs a separately authorized project, a connected repository and a named payer.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session at the existing pinned model pricing, 900 seconds, no managed-model routes of its own. The configured ceiling is not an expected price.

Work scales with the number of content files scanned and the size of the repository snapshot, not with link_budget. A large site costs more to search than a small one even when the answer is no_change.
One fetch of target_url plus the pinned repository workspace. No provider queries, no paid data.
effects: Opens one unmerged GitHub pull request touching at most 5 existing content files, each with one added link, or changes no files at all.
Writes one receipt at reports/internal-links/<run_id>.md in project state.
Never merges, pushes, deploys, or edits navigation, sitemaps, redirects, dependencies, tests, CI or deployment configuration. Nothing is live until a human merges.

cases.description: Two existing pages already use the target's phrase in ordinary prose; a third uses it only in a heading. Expect a pull request touching exactly the two, each naming its exact anchor phrase, and the heading-only page reported as rejected rather than edited.
Six pages contain an honest anchor and link_budget is 2. Expect exactly two files touched, chosen by the ranking, with the remaining candidates named as surfaced but not taken.

The phrase appears only inside code fences, an existing link and a heading. Expect a no-change result that says plainly the target still has no incoming links, with zero files changed and no invented sentence.
target_url returns 404. Expect a no-change result naming the status, never a link to a page that does not resolve.

rubric.question: Does every added link wrap wording that was already in the file, with no sentence rewritten, added or reordered?
Would a reader on each source page plausibly want to follow that link at that point in the text, rather than the phrase merely matching?
Does the pull-request body separate files changed, candidates rejected and unsupported files skipped, without implying fuller coverage than was achieved?
Are the checks actually run, and their results, stated separately from checks skipped and the reasons they were skipped?
